messages:
mike: Noticing an observability gap in the Python SDK: async client calls do not carry OpenTelemetry trace headers by default. Traces stop at our outbound call.

leah: Is this the same issue as the request-id middleware talk last sprint? sync vs async parity?

mike: Related. Sync client (requests) gets instrumented ok when users install requests-instrumentation, but our AsyncClient (httpx) path builds headers internally and ignores OTel context unless users manually inject.

carlos: Can you share a tiny repro? async or sync?

mike: Async, httpx backend. Minimal: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from opentelemetry import trace
client = AsyncClient(api_key="...")
tracer = trace.get_tracer("app")
async with tracer.start_as_current_span("span"):
    await client.chat.create("hi")
```
No traceparent header seen on egress.

leah: I dug into client/transport.py and it builds headers in a separate coroutine and falls back to env vars for X-Redwood-Request-Id. It never calls propagators.inject.

yana: Two clear asks: 1) automatic OTEL propagation (if opentelemetry installed) 2) middleware API so users can insert headers (request-id, tenant, etc).

carlos: Middleware should be both sync and async friendly. e.g. signature: (request: MutableMapping[str, str], next: Callable) -> Awaitable[Response] or Response. We'll need Protocols for typing.

mike: Also typing fix: streaming endpoints return generator-like objects but stubs use Any. Change to AsyncIterator[str] or AsyncIterator[TokenChunk]. MyPy CI fails on that across multiple repos.

leah: We should not import opentelemetry at top-level. Implement optional integration: redwood[otel] extras. At runtime, if module available, call propagators.inject(headers). Otherwise noop.

yana: UX: choose header names: prefer 'x-redwood-request-id' and 'traceparent' standard. Preserve user-supplied request-id if present. If not, generate uuid4 and surface in logs.

carlos: Quick workaround for users until we fix: they can call propagators.inject themselves and pass extra_headers param: 
```py
from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import inject
headers = {}
inject(headers)
await client.chat.create("hi", extra_headers=headers)
```
Not great but usable.

leah: Proposed API changes: 
- Client(..., propagate_tracing=True) default False for now, toggle to True in a major release
- Client.add_middleware(fn) where fn can mutate headers and either return next(request) or await it
- Types: define MiddlewareSync, MiddlewareAsync protocols and Request/Response TypedDicts

mike: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/427 adds middleware + optional otel propagation (WIP). Includes unit test harness that stubs httpx transport and asserts headers.

yana: CI bot triggered?

sdk-bot: Build started for PR #427 123f. Running tests (linux-py3.11, mypy).

carlos: For tests, use opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.InMemorySpanExporter and a test TracerProvider to assert a span exists and that propagator adds traceparent header to captured outgoing requests. 

leah: Don't forget to update docs: migration guide, examples for OTLP collector + sample async app showing both manual and auto propagation. Also show how to add a middleware that adds correlation ids from FastAPI request state.

mike: Agree. Also add a small e2e example in examples/otel-streaming.py that demonstrates streaming tokens with Typed streaming AsyncIterator and shows correlating logs with generated request-id.

yana: One more: ensure middleware order is deterministic (LIFO or FIFO?). I vote FIFO so first-added wraps later ones. Document that.

carlos: Will add that to RFC. Also ensure middleware errors don't swallow exceptions; surface them.

sdk-bot: PR #427 tests failed on mypy (streaming typing mismatch). Filing issue in CI job.

mike: I'll push fixes for types tonight. If anyone wants to pair on typing patterns for AsyncIterator, DM.

leah: Thanks all. Once PR passes tests we can cut a patch release and call out the opt-in flag, then flip default in next minor after migration window. :rocket:
